svg.text: OpenAI 948 Linux Kernel LPEs: Autonomous Pipeline & Patch Churn
Analysis of "A thousand fewer paths to root": multi-agent exploitation vs maintainer verification backlog
1. The Multi-Agent Exploitation Funnel (30h Run)
Automated analysis executed against Linux kernel master branch ($1.21M API cost)
Stage 1: Scout Agents (Target Reachability Filter)
• Scans 40M+ lines of kernel code for low-privilege entry points.
• Isolates 5,034 high-value audit targets (2.8M lines / ~7% of kernel).
Stage 2: Analyst Agents (Vulnerability Discovery)
• Models audit surfaces, checks bounds, concurrency, and refcounts.
• Flags 2,308 candidate defects across core subsystems and drivers.
Stage 3: Triage Agents (Dynamic KASAN VM Validation)
• Writes automated PoCs and runs them inside isolated QEMU VMs.
• Dynamically reproduces 1,724 live kernel crashes (74.7% hit rate).
Stage 4: Exploit Agents (Mitigation Defeat & Weaponization)
• Defeats KASLR, SMEP, and SMAP using 10 novel exploitation primitives.
• Yields 948 distinct working root exploits + 291 information leaks.
Stage 5: Patch Generation & Human-in-the-Loop Review
• Generates surgical C fixes; verifies exploit is neutralised in VM.
• Human team inspects diffs and coordinates responsible disclosures.
Economics: $1,213,430 total API credits => $1,279 per working LPE
2. Systemic Dilemma: The Maintenance Bottleneck
Why automated vulnerability scale overwhelms downstream infrastructure
10 Novel Exploitation Primitives Discovered
• 2 Persistent Elastic Objects: targeted SLUB/SLAB kernel cache spray.
• 2 Page-Grooming Methods: precise physical layout manipulation.
• 5 Data-Only Attacks: privilege escalation without CFI tripping.
The Upstream Review Crisis (Torvalds & Kroah-Hartman)
• Generating bugs is cheap; reviewing, backporting, and testing is costly.
• 948 fixes must be verified across 7 LTS kernel branches (5.10–7.2).
• Risk: Blind patch merging can trigger serious runtime regressions.
Distro Lag: Debian, RHEL, Ubuntu & Arch
• Downstream vendors cannot package 948 patches simultaneously.
• Unpatched servers leave an open operational window for local attackers.
• Threat: Local user or container break-in = instant root escalation.
Architectural Defense: Stop Relying on Shared Kernels
• Restrict unprivileged namespaces: kernel.unprivileged_userns_clone=0
• Disable unprivileged eBPF: kernel.unprivileged_bpf_disabled=2
• Replace bare containers with MicroVMs (Firecracker, Kata, gVisor).
• Principle: Assume any local user or tenant has immediate root capability.
